title: Stability Coordinator Playbook & Phase Plan — Reliability SLO Program
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the Stability Coordinator to run a cross-functional program that establishes service-level objectives (SLOs) across Redwood’s core inference surfaces. The doc is intentionally pragmatic — a mix of runbook, project plan, checklist and meeting notes. Aim: get from discovery to pilot to org-wide SLO rollouts with clearly assigned owners, measurable SLIs, and an error-budget process that teams can adopt within 6 months.

Audience:
- SRE leads and individual contributors
- Platform and serving runtime engineers
- Product managers for Hosted API, Dedicated, Private
- Observability/Monitoring and Developer Experience teams
- Solutions & Professional Services (for customer-facing SLAs)

High-level constraints and assumptions:
- We prioritize user-facing latency, request success, and model correctness signals as first-class SLO families.
- No broad instrumentation rewrite upfront; prefer adapter layers and sampling to limit scope.
- Pilots run on two services: Hosted API text generation (api-gen) and Dedicated routing (ded-router).
- Error budget enforcement must be automatable via CI/CD gates where possible.

Phase plan (summary):
- Phase 0 — Prep & Discovery (4 weeks): inventory SLIs, gap analysis, lightweight instrumentation, stakeholder alignment.
- Phase 1 — Pilot (8 weeks): implement SLIs on api-gen, define SLOs, surface dashboards and alerting, run 1-month trial.
- Phase 2 — Cross-team Rollout (12 weeks): roll SLO patterns to ded-router and one additional product, implement automated error-budget policies, runbooks, and cadence.
- Phase 3 — Operationalize (ongoing): SLO governance, periodic review, onboarding templates, training.

Detailed activities by phase:
Phase 0 — Prep & Discovery (owners and deliverables):
- Inventory: compile list of all production endpoints and perceived user journeys (Owner: Maya) — deliverable: endpoint-catalog.csv.
- Baseline telemetry: capture current SLI coverage and gaps (Owner: Priya) — deliverable: instrumentation-gap-matrix.md.
- Stakeholder kickoff: run a 90-min alignment session with PMs + Platform + Observability (Owner: Liam) — deliverable: alignment-decisions.log.
- Risk & compliance check: surface PII/consent issues for observability (Owner: Sofia) — deliverable: compliance-note.pdf.

Phase 1 — Pilot (api-gen)
- SLI definitions (examples):
  - Request success rate: proportion of requests returning 200-level responses excluding client-cancelled (SLI window: rolling 28d).
  - 95th percentile end-to-end latency (inference start -> final token emitted) for requests under 2s target path.
  - Model quality proxy: regression signal based on a small canonical prompt set that measures token-level perplexity delta and hallucination heuristics (daily).
- Target SLOs (pilot suggestions):
  - Success rate: 99.95% per 28 day window.
  - P95 latency: <= 600ms for p99 users on hosted regions (measured on production traffic).
  - Quality pass rate on canonical set: >= 98% (with automated alerts on regression >1.5%).
- Implementation tasks:
  - Instrument success/latency metrics via the metrics adapter (Owner: Priya) — add tags for route/model/version.
  - Wire QoE regression job into nightly pipelines (Owner: Diego).
  - Create dashboards: SLO health, error budget burn, per-model breakdown (Owner: Observability team).
  - Create a canary policy document for model rollouts tied to error budget usage (Owner: Product/PM).
- Pilot evaluation: 4-week observation window after initial 2-week stabilization. Success criteria to promote to Phase 2: stable instrumentation, <5% false-positive alerts, and actionable runbook for at least two high-frequency incidents.

Phase 2 — Cross-team rollout (ded-router + one more)
- Standardize SLO templates: SLI definition language (OpenMetrics naming), dashboards, alert thresholds, runbook skeletons (Owner: SRE Platform).
- Automate enforcement: integrate error-budget checks into CI gating for infra changes and model deploys (Owner: Release Eng).
- Training & onboarding: 2x 60-min workshops for teams adopting template (Owner: Maya + DevEx).
- Customer-facing commitments: working with Solutions to map internal SLOs to customer SLAs for Dedicated customers (Owner: Solutions Eng).

Phase 3 — Operationalize
- Quarterly SLO review board (participants: SRE, Product PMs, Observability, Solutions) to review SLO adjustments and policy exceptions.
- SLO registry: lightweight Confluence page per service with canonical SLI definitions and ownership.
- Continual improvements: periodic sampling calibration, adding A/B experiments to measure user-perceived impact vs budget enforcement.

Roles & responsibilities (practical model):
- Stability Coordinator (Maya): run the program, maintain phase plan, drive cross-team cadence, escalate unresolved blockers.
- Service Owner (product/infra): owns SLO choices for their product surface, approves targets.
- Instrumentation Lead (Priya): ensures metrics correctness, schema, spans.
- Observability Lead: builds dashboards, maintains alert rules, defines measurement windows.
- Release/Deploy Lead: enforces pre-deploy error budget checks and rollback criteria.
- Solutions/Customer Success: translates SLOs to customer communications and contract needs.

Error budget policy (proposal):
- Burn definitions: daily burn rate compared to linear budget; triggers at 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% burn thresholds.
- Automated responses: at 50% -> post-mortem review scheduled; at 75% -> pause risky deploys (non-security), at 100% -> automatic hold on model weight updates and escalation to incident commander.
- Exception handling: documented exceptions require explicit sign-off from SRE manager + Product lead.

Measurement & instrumentation checklist:
- Metrics: success_rate, latency_p50/p95/p99, model_quality_regression, client_cancel_rate.
- Tags: service, route, model_id, region, deployment_id.
- Sampling: 100% sampling for success/latency metrics for 30 days after rollout, then drop to 10% if ingestion costs are a concern.
- Log retention: short tail retention for detailed traces (14 days) with aggregated long-term indices for SLO dashboards (90 days).

Dashboards & alerts (must-haves):
- SLO health: current % vs target, 28d window, sparkline 90d.
- Error budget burn: 1d, 7d, 28d burn visualization.
- Top contributing errors: grouped by route/model/version.
- On-call alert: when burn exceeds 75% (severity P2) and when absolute SLO violated for > 1 hour (severity P1).

Communications and cadence:
- Weekly stability sync (30m) for Phase 1 between SRE/Platform/Obs/Product.
- Bi-weekly governance meeting during Phase 2 for rollout decisions.
- Post-incident templates: short summary, root cause, mitigation, follow-up tasks, updated runbook link.

Rollout & release controls (example):
- Canary rule: 5% of traffic for 24 hours, no SLO violation and no more than 10% of normal error budget burn.
- Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over configurable windows only if canary green.
- Fallback: automatic traffic reroute to previous model variant on P1-class conditions.

Success metrics for the program (OKRs):
- O1: 95% of core product routes have SLOs defined and instrumented by end of Q2.
- O2: Pilot services show <1% unexpected SLA regressions after 3 months.
- O3: At least two deployments aborted by error-budget gating avoided a major outage (prevented ROI story).

Risks & open questions:
- Risk: telemetry cost growth. Mitigation: aggressive sampling strategy + cardinality limits.
- Risk: model quality SLI is noisy. Mitigation: combine synthetic canonical set with production holdout scoring.
- Open: what constitutes a customer-impacting hallucination for quantifying quality SLO? Need product/legal alignment.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Run the stakeholder kickoff (Owner: Maya) — goal: approve pilot criteria and pilot services.
- Priya to publish instrumentation-gap-matrix and start metric tags review.
- Diego to prototype nightly QoE regression job on sample dataset.

Action items tracker (short):
- Maya: schedule kickoff and prepare slide deck (due: 2025-10-24).
- Priya: initial metric naming proposal merged to infra-metrics (due: 2025-11-03).
- Diego: QoE job PoC in CI with daily report (due: 2025-11-10).
- Liam: draft canary policy and add to release playbooks (due: 2025-11-05).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep pilot small; prove the loop — instrumentation -> dashboard -> alert -> runbook -> post-mortem.
- Expect pushback on targets; focus on measurable tradeoffs and historical baselines.
- Keep communications low-friction: automated weekly email digest of SLO health per service.

Appendix: example SLO YAML (informal sketch)
- service: api-gen
  sli: request_success_rate
  window: 28d
  objective: 0.9995
  measurement: exclude_client_cancels: true
  owner: eng-api

(End of working doc)
